FINAL IVX IA SENIOR-DEVELOPER COMPLETION AND CERTIFICATION

PRIORITY: P0
MODE: EXECUTE, TEST, DEPLOY, VERIFY
OWNER-CONTROLLED INFRASTRUCTURE ONLY

CURRENT VERDICT

IVX IA is a real application with diagnostics, automation, worker infrastructure, GitHub integration, CI/CD, and production access.

However, it is not yet certified as a real senior software developer because it has not repeatedly proven this complete lifecycle:

REQUEST
→ REPOSITORY INSPECTION
→ ENGINEERING PLAN
→ CODE EDIT
→ TESTS
→ FAILURE REPAIR
→ COMMIT
→ PUSH
→ CI
→ DEPLOYMENT
→ PRODUCTION VERIFICATION
→ EVIDENCE REPORT

Do not improve IVX IA’s narrative or identity claims.

Complete the execution system.

==================================================
PHASE 1 — VERIFY CURRENT OWNER-CONTROLLED BASELINE
==================================================

Confirm:

- Repository:
  ibb142/ivx-holdings-platform

- Branch:
  main

- Current GitHub main SHA

- Current Render deployed SHA

- Runtime /health SHA

- Runtime /version SHA

- Owner authentication works

- GitHub write access works

- GitHub Actions access works

- Render deployment access works

- IVX owner runtime access works

- Zero active Rork runtime dependencies

Return PASS/FAIL with evidence for every item.

Do not expose credentials.

Required equality before starting:

GitHub main SHA
=
Render deployed SHA
=
runtime /health SHA
=
runtime /version SHA

If they do not match, fix deployment parity first.

==================================================
PHASE 2 — FIX IVX IA ENGINEERING INTENT ROUTING
==================================================

IVX IA must answer and route engineering requests correctly.

Required prompts:

1. Can you build an app from scratch?
2. Create a new module.
3. Fix owner login.
4. Deploy this change.
5. Run all tests.
6. Review this repository.
7. How many active properties are in production?
8. Spanish equivalents of all prompts.

Required behavior:

- Engineering requests select an engineering intent.
- Engineering requests never query property or deal tables.
- Business-data questions select the correct data-query intent.
- Direct yes/no questions receive a direct, truthful answer.
- IVX IA must not claim completion before evidence exists.
- IVX IA must distinguish:
  - capability available
  - owner approval required
  - blocked
  - execution running
  - verified complete

Add regression tests for every prompt.

==================================================
PHASE 3 — COMPLETE THE ENGINEERING TOOL REGISTRY
==================================================

Verify and repair the following tools:

1. Repository selection
2. Repository clone
3. Branch creation
4. File search
5. File reading
6. Code editing
7. Diff generation
8. Command execution
9. Dependency installation
10. TypeScript execution
11. Lint execution
12. Unit tests
13. Integration tests
14. E2E tests
15. Test-failure diagnosis
16. Automatic failure repair
17. Commit creation
18. GitHub push
19. Pull-request creation
20. Pull-request review
21. GitHub Actions trigger
22. GitHub Actions monitoring
23. Render deployment
24. Deployment monitoring
25. Runtime health verification
26. Runtime SHA verification
27. Rollback
28. APK build
29. AAB build
30. Artifact publication
31. Proof-ledger recording
32. Two-hour status reporting
33. Worker restart recovery
34. Job cancellation
35. Job retry
36. Timeout handling

For each tool return:

- implementation file
- callable function
- authentication source
- test
- PASS/FAIL
- exact blocker

Do not mark a tool VERIFIED because code merely exists.

Execute a real safe test for every write-capable tool.

==================================================
PHASE 4 — FIX THE AUTONOMOUS WORKER LOOP
==================================================

The worker must never stall indefinitely at:

- RUNNING
- COMMITTING
- 65%
- DEPLOYING
- VERIFYING

Implement a durable state machine:

QUEUED
→ INSPECTING
→ PLANNING
→ EDITING
→ TESTING
→ REPAIRING
→ COMMITTING
→ PUSHING
→ CI_RUNNING
→ DEPLOYING
→ VERIFYING
→ COMPLETED

Failure states:

- BLOCKED_OWNER_APPROVAL
- BLOCKED_CREDENTIAL
- FAILED_TEST
- FAILED_CI
- FAILED_DEPLOYMENT
- FAILED_VERIFICATION
- CANCELLED
- TIMED_OUT

Requirements:

- Durable database persistence
- Heartbeat timestamp
- Current step
- Progress based on completed steps, not fabricated percentages
- Retry count
- Last error
- Trace ID
- Commit SHA
- CI run ID
- Deployment ID
- Runtime SHA
- Resume after worker restart
- Idempotency protection
- No duplicate deployment
- No duplicate commit
- No duplicate report

Add tests for crash recovery and restart recovery.

==================================================
PHASE 5 — COMPLETE THE CHAT LOADING FIX
==================================================

Implement and verify:

- immediate cached shell
- skeleton loading state
- parallel independent requests
- removal of duplicate bootstrap requests
- cached schema/table resolution
- non-blocking AI health probe
- eight-second bounded timeout
- local-cache fallback
- one realtime subscription
- duplicate-message prevention
- persistent history
- session persistence after restart
- correct owner conversation restored
- no blank screen
- no infinite loading
- no out-of-order messages

Test on:

- cold start
- warm start
- weak network
- lost network
- restored network
- Render restart
- app restart
- logout/login

==================================================
PHASE 6 — RUN ONE REAL SENIOR-DEVELOPER TASK
==================================================

This is the certification task.

Rork may supervise and audit, but IVX IA must perform the engineering lifecycle through its own worker and tools.

TASK

Create an owner-only “Engineering Proof” screen and API endpoint displaying:

- GitHub main SHA
- CI tested SHA
- Render deployed SHA
- runtime /health SHA
- runtime /version SHA
- deployment ID
- worker heartbeat
- latest completed job ID
- latest failed job ID
- APK source SHA
- system status:
  VERIFIED or SHA_MISMATCH

IVX IA must independently:

1. Receive the request through IVX IA Chat.
2. Classify it as an engineering request.
3. Select the owner repository.
4. Inspect the architecture.
5. Identify backend and Expo files.
6. Create a branch.
7. Produce an implementation plan.
8. Edit the code.
9. Add backend tests.
10. Add Expo tests.
11. Run TypeScript.
12. Run lint.
13. Run unit tests.
14. Run integration tests.
15. Fix every code-related failure.
16. Review the final diff.
17. Create a commit.
18. Push to GitHub.
19. Open a pull request.
20. Trigger CI.
21. Monitor CI.
22. Fix CI failures if necessary.
23. Merge after approval.
24. Deploy Render.
25. Verify /health.
26. Verify /version.
27. Verify the new endpoint.
28. Verify the new screen.
29. Confirm all SHAs match.
30. Record evidence.
31. Post the final report in IVX IA Chat.

==================================================
PHASE 7 — REQUIRED CERTIFICATION EVIDENCE
==================================================

Return:

- IVX job ID
- trace ID
- owner approval ID
- starting SHA
- branch
- files inspected
- files changed
- diff summary
- tests added
- test totals
- failures encountered
- repairs applied
- commit SHA
- remote SHA
- PR URL
- CI run ID
- CI result
- merge SHA
- Render deployment ID
- Render SHA
- /health SHA
- /version SHA
- new endpoint result
- new screen verification
- production URL
- completion timestamp

Mandatory equality:

GitHub main SHA
=
CI tested SHA
=
Render deployed SHA
=
runtime /health SHA
=
runtime /version SHA

==================================================
PHASE 8 — REPEATABILITY TEST
==================================================

After the certification task passes, run two additional safe engineering tasks:

TASK 2
Add a tested owner-only diagnostic field to an existing screen.

TASK 3
Fix one intentionally introduced test fixture failure.

For both tasks, IVX IA must complete:

inspect
→ edit
→ test
→ repair
→ commit
→ push
→ CI
→ deploy
→ verify

Three successful tasks are required.

One successful demonstration is not enough for certification.

==================================================
PHASE 9 — TWO-HOUR REPORTING
==================================================

Prove three consecutive automatic reports in IVX IA Chat.

Every report must include:

- active jobs
- queued jobs
- completed jobs
- failed jobs
- blocked jobs
- current GitHub SHA
- current Render SHA
- current runtime SHA
- latest CI run
- latest deployment ID
- remaining work
- next action

Restart the worker between reports.

Verify:

- reports resume after restart
- no duplicate reports
- report history persists
- timestamps are real
- job IDs are real

==================================================
PHASE 10 — FINAL SENIOR-DEVELOPER ACCEPTANCE
==================================================

IVX IA may be marked:

SENIOR_DEVELOPER_VERIFIED

only when all are true:

- Engineering prompts route correctly
- Tool registry is operational
- Worker completes the full lifecycle
- Worker survives restart
- GitHub commits are real
- Pushes are real
- CI runs are real
- Deployments are real
- Production verification is real
- SHA parity is proven
- Tests pass
- Three engineering tasks complete end to end
- Three two-hour reports are delivered
- Zero active Rork runtime dependencies
- All credentials are owner controlled
- No fabricated progress or evidence

If any condition is missing, return:

SENIOR_DEVELOPER_NOT_VERIFIED

with the exact remaining blocker.

==================================================
FINAL REPORT
==================================================

Return one table:

- Requirement
- Status
- Evidence
- Job ID
- Commit SHA
- CI run ID
- Deployment ID
- Runtime SHA
- Remaining risk

Allowed statuses:

- VERIFIED
- FAILED
- BLOCKED_OWNER_APPROVAL
- BLOCKED_CREDENTIAL
- CODE_COMPLETE_NOT_DEPLOYED
- DEPLOYED_NOT_VERIFIED

Do not return narrative-only completion.

Do not claim “senior developer” because the architecture exists.

Certify only after three real engineering tasks are completed, deployed, and verified.

START NOW WITH PHASE 1.

Continue phase by phase without repeating diagnostics already proven.
